citation: S. Bosch and W. Lütkebohmert, Stable Reduction and Uniformization of Abelian Varieties I, Math. Ann. 270 (1985), 349–379
statement_checked: Every smooth geometrically connected projective curve over a complete nontrivially valued non-Archimedean field has potential stable reduction when its genus is at least two, and potential semistable reduction when its genus is at most one.
proof_text_read: Machine OCR of printed pages 374–378; theorem statement and the displayed genus inequalities and prime-to-residue-characteristic choice independently checked on the scan.
ocr_corrections: The genus conditions are g(C)≤1 and g(C)≥1, rather than OCR strict/reversed symbols.
The auxiliary integer is prime to the residue characteristic, rather than the characteristic of the valued field.
unclosed_proof_dependencies: Earlier semistable-model, formal-fibre and genus formulas have not all been independently reconstructed.
The elementary affinoid subdomains of projective-line step in the proof is omitted by the source and must be supplied when required.
The conversion to the exact affinoid-domain/formal-boundary realization used by the curve draft is a separate obligation.
